newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, June 16 - Puerto Cortes - Six vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers, 3 discharging (1 corn, 1 asphalt, 1 potash). 3 Vessels awaiting berths of which 1 to discharge/load containers, 2 to discharge (1 wheat, 1 ammonium sulphate). 15 Vessels due of which 8 to load/discharge (7 containers, 1 passengers/vehicles). 7 To discharge (5 bananas, 1 rebars, 1 corn). Port congested. Puerto Cortes - Five vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/general cargo. 3 Discharging (1 corn, 2 fertiliser). 3 Vessels at anchorage of which 2 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 1 to discharge asphalt. 20 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 12 to discharge/load containers/general cargo, 6 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load lumber.

MEXICO, June 18 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Eight vessels in port of which 3 general cargo, 3 minerals, 2 dmt. Altamira - One vessel in port under repair. Veracruz - 17 Vessels in port of which 1 aluminium, 2 steel coils, 1 scrap, 3 containers, 6 grain, 1 minerals, 3 sugar. Manzanillo - Seven vessels in port of which 2 containers, 1 steel coils, 2 fruit, 2 oil tankers. Coatzacoalcos - 18 Vessels in port of which 9 oil tankers, 8 chemicals, 1 under repair.

PANAMA, June 16 - Cristobal, Balboa - Working normally. Panama Canal - Working at full capacity. 43 Vessels due, 32 in queue, 13 booked, 42 due. Conditions 15/6, actual arrivals 35, transits 36. Average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 19.1 hours.

UNITED STATES, June 16 - Jersey City - Two vessels in port. Port Newark - Five vessels in port. Port Elizabeth - Two vessels in port. Perth Amboy - One vessel in port. Bayway - Cartaret - No vessels. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion/delays. Hampton Roads, VA - Three general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating. 2 Vessels berthed loading coal, 1 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker loading fertiliser, 1 discharging cement, 1 tanker discharging fuel oil, 1 parcel tanker discharging caustic soda. 4 Vessels berthed under repair/lay-berth.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. Clear C.D canal/Baltimore harbour. Elevators and coal operations working well, with no delays. Average waiting time at Console Coal is 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities operating normal, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC. - No vessels due at either shipyard, river, coal terminal or the grain elevator over the next week. No delays expected at tanker terminals. All terminals working normally. Charleston, Columbus Street, north Charleston and Wando terminal will be light. Dredging continues in main channel with no navigational problems.

Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berthing congestion or delays for the ports of Jacksonville or Fernanda Beach, FL. Miami, FL - Traffic is expected to be normal at the ports of Miami and Port Everglades. New York, NY - Congestion in New York Stapleton anchorage and congestion in tanker terminals. No congestion in Bay Ridge anchorage and sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier expecting 17 vessels during this week. At present, 2 vessels are anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal is expecting 10 vessels. Pier IX terminal is expecting 6 vessels during the next week. Southern Coal pier 6 will undertake a maintenance period from 10-31/7 to perform work on one of the ship loaders. During this period, one loader will be working. Cargill is not expecting any vessels during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals are working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals are all working normally. All channels are open, with prevailing depths available.

Philadelphia, PA - No congestion in the ports of Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No activity as far as dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - Garden City terminals are forecasting a steady week for the entire period. Ocean terminals are also forecasting a steady week, with no delays expected. East coast terminal is forecasting a steady week but no delays. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility expects delays as vessels continue to wait at anchor. Savannah sugar refinery will be rather slow, with only one barge expected. All bulk liquid facilities are operating normally with no congestion expected. Navigational conditions remain normal. Weather conditions are seasonal. As the weather warms, afternoon thunderstorms may cause some downtime on weather sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - Port congested for vessels requiring open docks. This will last until next week. Congestion also exists in some oil/chemical terminals and private terminals for break bulk cargo such as Greensport and Manchester. Farmland grain elevator at Galveston is now back in full operation. Public grain elevator and Cargill are open with no delays. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rains occurring which may cause delays in cargo operation, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 11.6 ft. and expected to rise to 12.2 ft. by 16 June. High river conditions will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 46 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 45 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Based on these drafts, we would advise all vessels to maintain sufficient air-draft for transit under bridges in Miss

WEST COAST - Columbia river - The Columbia river district continues to experience high river levels. In fact river levels have not been this high since 1972. This continues to disrupt loading operations at certain terminals, and is also slowing transits up and down Columbia river district. Grain activity continues slow with 10 grain vessels in the Columbia river.

Average waiting period 1-3 days at most terminals. Coos Bay, OR - The past week has been slow. Two vessels in port at present, one discharging nickel ore at Glenbrook nickel terminal and one vessel loading lumber for Australia discharge. Due to arrive are three wood-chip carriers, all due at Roseburg dock next week and it appears at least two of the vessels will be confronted with some berthing congestion. A full load (3.9 m scribner) log vessel is also scheduled to call later next week, loading for various Japanese discharge ports. No delays in vessel traffic due to weather conditions.

Honolulu, HI - Pier 10/11 will no longer be available on Saturdays for berthing. Other vessels due to return of m/v independence to Hawaii service. BHP has increased its in port bunkering operations at piers 32-34 Honolulu harbour. Mgo/o can now be taken by pipeline. The increase in vessels calling at the pipelines for fuel has caused some short delays, but the BHP scheduler and harbour master have been working closely to keep the ships moving. Long Beach, CA, Los Angeles, CA - Congestion may be expected in the last week of June, particularly at Long Beach berths 212/214 bulk coal terminals. 5 July on this day there will be no work performed from 08.00 hrs. 5/7 until 07.00 hrs. 6/7. A new coal terminal has opened at the port of Los Angeles and the first coal rail-cars arrived at the new laxt (Los Angeles export terminal, berth 301) this past week. First staging of coal for actual export shipments is expected during late July. The first vessel may be loaded late September/early October.
